findings.claim: The public GET /groups/:name/members endpoint now defaults to limit=50 for every group, but the public route and template have no pagination controls, so members after the 50th cannot be reached.

verifier.reason: The patch changes groups_controller.rb `members` so every group defaults to `limit = (params[:limit] || 50)`; before, only automatic groups were limited, to 200. The public group-members.js.es6 route only calls `model.findMembers()`, which sends the model's default limit 50 and offset 0. members.hbs, group.js.es6 and the missing group-members controller/view have no next, previous or load-more control, so the public page can never show members after the 50th.

findings.claim: In the group member row itemView, {{#unless automatic}} resolves against the member (Discourse.User) rather than the group, so `automatic` is undefined and the remove link is shown for automatic groups.

verifier.reason: group.hbs:170 uses the keyword form `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}`. In the bundled Ember 1.9 (vendor/assets/javascripts/development/ember.js:7997-7998), that form binds each item view's context to `_parentView.context`, which is the admin-group ObjectController, so `automatic` in group_member.hbs:1 resolves to the group's flag and not to the member. That is also why the template has to name `member` explicitly.

findings.claim: The item-view template references `member`, but that alias is not available inside a separate itemView template, so rows render without member data and remove can fail when the controller calls member.get(...).

verifier.reason: Ember's EachView.createChildView (vendor/assets/javascripts/development/ember.js:8217-8224) writes the `member` alias into each item view's own keywords (`view._keywords[keyword] = content`). So group_member.hbs:1 can resolve `member` inside the `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}` rows created at group.hbs:170, and the rows and the removeMember action get the actual user.

findings.claim: A function has code paths that end without an explicit return and return undefined.

verifier.reason: The claim holds, though it causes no bug. Several functions can return undefined: the new `findMembers` early exit is now a bare `return ;` where it used to return `Ember.RSVP.resolve([])` (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:21). The new `addMembers` action ends without a return statement (admin-group.js.es6:87-91), and `userCountDisplay` returns nothing when the count is 0 or less (group.js:14-18). No caller uses the result of `findMembers` (both routes and group.js:47,58 call it and ignore it), so nothing breaks today.

findings.claim: The group[usernames] parameter is now ignored by the API.

verifier.reason: After the patch, Admin::GroupsController#create and #update (app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:22-47) read only the top-level params[:name], params[:visible] and params[:alias_level]. Nothing reads params[:group] or sets group.usernames, so an API client that sends group[usernames] gets a success response but membership doesn't change; members can now only be changed through the new add_members and remove_member actions (lines 49-80).

findings.claim: The admin group create and update actions read top-level params instead of group[...], with no compatibility path: legacy create gets a blank name (422) and legacy update silently sets visible=false.

verifier.reason: In app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb, create (patch lines 541-544) now reads params[:name] and params[:visible], and update (580-583) reads params[:alias_level], params[:visible] and params[:name]; neither looks at params[:group] any more. A legacy create sending group[name] gets name '' and fails UsernameValidator, so render_json_error returns 422. A legacy update hits `params[:visible] == "true"`, which is false when the field is missing, so visible is silently set to false. The in-repo JS client (group.js asJSON) was updated in the same patch, so only outside API callers break.

findings.claim: GET /groups/:name/members now returns {members, meta} instead of an array, which is not backwards compatible.

verifier.reason: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:28-35 now returns `{members: [...], meta: {total, limit, offset}}`, where it used to return a bare array (`render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)`). The patch updates all in-repo callers (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:25), but any outside API client that expects an array will break.

findings.claim: The PATCH /admin/groups/:id endpoint with changes[add|delete] is removed without documentation.

verifier.reason: The patch deletes `update_patch` and the `request.patch?` branch in `app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb` (old lines 539-564 and 595-596) and the PATCH incremental specs. The patch has no changelog or deprecation note. `resources :groups` (`config/routes.rb:45`) still sends PATCH to `update`, which ignores `changes` and returns success. Because `params[:visible]` is missing from such a request, `update` also sets `visible` to false.

findings.claim: The '== 0' comparisons at lines 7 and 12 violate the .jshintrc eqeqeq rule.

verifier.reason: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:7 and :12 both use `this.get("user_count") == 0`, and .jshintrc:61 sets `"eqeqeq": true`. The `eqnull` option (.jshintrc:79) only allows `== null`, so these comparisons break the rule; the default *.js lint globs may not pick up .es6 files.

findings.claim: totalPages is computed as Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, which gives one extra page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 100/50 gives 3), so navigation can reach an empty page.

verifier.reason: admin-group.js.es6:19 (patch line 19) computes totalPages as Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1, so 100/50 gives 3. With offset 50, currentPage is 2, which is not equal to totalPages, so showingLast is false (line 23). The `next` action (lines 58-61) then sets offset to min(100, 100) = 100, which loads an empty page 3.

findings.claim: The next action clamps the offset to user_count instead of the last valid offset, so it can navigate to an empty page (e.g. total equal to limit gives offset == total).

verifier.reason: In admin-group.js.es6:59, `next` clamps the offset to `Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)`. Lines 17-20 compute `totalPages = floor(user_count/limit) + 1`, so with user_count == limit (e.g. 50/50) the controller reports 2 pages, `showingLast` is false on page 1, and `next` sets offset = 50 = user_count, which loads an empty page.

findings.claim: remove_member uses group.users.delete(user_id), which bypasses callbacks so the groups.user_count counter_cache is not decremented, unlike add_members which uses group.add.

verifier.reason: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:649 (patch line 649) calls group.users.delete(user_id) on `has_many :users, through: :group_users` (app/models/group.rb:8). Under Rails 4.1.8 (Gemfile.lock:307) this removes the GroupUser join rows with delete_all and skips callbacks, so the `counter_cache: "user_count"` on GroupUser (app/models/group_user.rb:2) is not decremented. add_members goes through group.add, which calls users.push (group.rb:272-273) and creates the GroupUser normally, so the count goes up; the existing Group#remove (group.rb:276-277) destroys each row and would keep the count right.

findings.claim: remove_member uses group.users.delete(user_id) instead of Group#remove, so the removed user's primary_group_id is not cleared and the group can still show as post flair.

verifier.reason: The new remove_member action in app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb (patch line 649) calls group.users.delete(user_id) and never clears User.primary_group_id. Before this patch, removing someone through usernames= went through Group#destroy_deletions (app/models/group.rb:287-291), which did clear it, and post_serializer.rb:96-102 still shows that group as the user's flair. One part of the claim is wrong: Group#remove (group.rb:276-278) does not clear primary_group_id either, so switching to it would not fix this.

findings.claim: add_members calls usernames.split(','), assuming a string; usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b yields an Array and raises NoMethodError (500).

verifier.reason: In the patched GroupsController#add_members, `params.require(:usernames)` is followed by `usernames.split(",")` with no type check. With `usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b`, ActiveSupport's Array#split returns `[["a","b"]]`, so it is `User.find_by_username` (app/models/user.rb:176, `username.downcase`) that raises NoMethodError, not split itself; the request still ends in a 500.

findings.claim: The 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' controller spec sends xhr :put to remove_member, but the route is DELETE; it passes only because controller specs skip routing.

verifier.reason: The spec added by the patch calls `xhr :put, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42` (change.patch ~line 952). The route only allows DELETE: `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` (config/routes.rb:49), and `put "members"` goes to add_members (routes.rb:50). Controller specs call the action directly and don't check that the HTTP verb matches the route, so the spec passes anyway.

findings.claim: The limit and offset params on the members endpoint are not validated or clamped: negative values reach SQL and cause errors, and limit has no upper cap.

verifier.reason: At app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22-26, `limit` and `offset` come straight from `params` via `.to_i` and go into `.limit(limit).offset(offset)` without being clamped. Negative values reach Postgres, which rejects them ('LIMIT/OFFSET must not be negative') and the request returns a 500. There is also no upper cap, so a request with a huge `limit` returns all members.

findings.claim: findMembers() is called asynchronously without its promise being returned or awaited from setupController, so the template may render before member data is available.

verifier.reason: The patch removes the afterModel hooks that returned model.findMembers(). In admin_group_route.js setupController (patch line 127) and group-members.js.es6 setupController (patch line 364), `model.findMembers();` is now called without its promise being returned or awaited, so the route renders before members load. The members are set on the model through setProperties, so the template fills in once the request finishes. The visible effect is an empty list at first, and any request error is not handled.

findings.claim: removeMember and addMembers have no rejection handler, so 422/500 responses give the admin no feedback.

verifier.reason: The patch adds Group.removeMember and addMembers in app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js. Each one chains only .then() onto Discourse.ajax, and neither the model nor the controller actions in admin-group.js.es6 attach a catch or rejection handler. Discourse.ajax (discourse/mixins/ajax.js:51-67) only rejects on error and shows no message of its own, so a 422 or 500 response fails silently.

findings.claim: The usernames input is not cleared after an add operation.

verifier.reason: In app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:61-65, the addMembers action calls model.addMembers(usernames) but never resets `usernames`, and a `// TODO: should clear the input` comment admits it. model.addMembers in discourse/models/group.js only reloads the member list, so the user-selector bound to `usernames` (group.hbs) still shows the names after the add.

findings.claim: add_members calls group.add(user) without checking for existing membership, so adding an existing member violates the unique index on group_users(group_id,user_id) and raises RecordNotUnique (500), and earlier users stay committed because there is no transaction.

verifier.reason: Admin::GroupsController#add_members (app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb, patch lines 622-626) calls group.add(user) for each username without checking whether the user is already a member. Group#add is `self.users.push(user)` (app/models/group.rb:272-274), which immediately inserts a GroupUser row for a saved group. GroupUser has no uniqueness validation (app/models/group_user.rb), and the (group_id,user_id) index is UNIQUE (db/migrate/20130416004933_group_users.rb:9), so adding an existing member raises RecordNotUnique (a 500), and users inserted earlier in the loop stay saved because there is no surrounding transaction.

findings.claim: Removing the last member on the last page leaves an empty page because findMembers keeps the old offset.

verifier.reason: In discourse/models/group.js:259, findMembers caps the offset using the local user_count, which still holds the count from before the removal. With limit 50 and 51 members, removing the only member on page 2 refetches with offset 50. The server returns no members and meta.offset 50 (groups_controller.rb:686-698), and admin-group.js.es6:12-20 then shows page 2/2 with an empty list.

findings.claim: The pending 'ensures that membership can be paginated' spec still parses the old array shape, and no spec covers the new {members, meta} response contract.

verifier.reason: spec/controllers/groups_controller_spec.rb:72-84 is still marked `pending` and reads `JSON.parse(response.body)` as an array of users, but the patch changes GroupsController#members to return `{members: [...], meta: {total, limit, offset}}` (change.patch lines 692-699). The patch leaves this spec untouched and adds no other spec or JS test for the new response shape.

findings.claim: group.save with render_json_error after add/remove is effectively a no-op, because membership writes already hit the DB via has_many :through, so the error branch only fires on unrelated group validation failures.

verifier.reason: For an already-saved group, `Group#add` (app/models/group.rb:272-274) calls `users.push` on the `has_many :through` association (group.rb:8), and `remove_member` calls `group.users.delete(user_id)`. Both write the join rows to the database straight away. The later `group.save` in `add_members`/`remove_member` (app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:616-656) therefore saves no membership changes, and `render_json_error` can only fire on the group's own validations (group.rb:12-13, 37).

findings.claim: addMembers ends with '})' without a semicolon, which triggers jshint W033 under .jshintrc.

verifier.reason: In app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:59, the return statement in addMembers ends with '})' and no semicolon. .jshintrc does not set asi, and its 'lastsemic: true' only allows a missing semicolon when the closing brace is on the same line, which it is not here (line 60), so jshint raises W033 'Missing semicolon'.

findings.claim: There is a stray semicolon after a block (if (!this.get('id')) { return };), which triggers jshint W032.

verifier.reason: The patch adds `if (!this.get('id')) { return };` at app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:82 (patch line 339). The semicolon after the closing brace of the block is an empty statement, which jshint reports as W032 "Unnecessary semicolon".

findings.claim: The routes provide the group id in params[:id], but the controller reads params[:group_id], causing a param-missing failure.

verifier.reason: In config/routes.rb:49-50, `delete "members"` and `put "members"` sit directly inside the `resources :groups` block, not inside a `member do` block. Rails therefore treats them as nested routes, `/admin/groups/:group_id/members`, so `params.require(:group_id)` in app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:617 and :644 reads the right key.

findings.claim: The Group#usernames= setter, destroy_deletions and after_save :destroy_deletions are now dead code in production; only specs call the setter.

verifier.reason: The patch deletes the only production callers of the setter, `group.usernames = payload[:usernames]` and the one in `create` (change.patch:577, :609). After that, `usernames=` (app/models/group.rb:244) is assigned only in spec/models/group_spec.rb:149,153 and spec/models/user_spec.rb:1011,1022, so `@deletions` is never set and `destroy_deletions` (group.rb:287, run via `after_save` at group.rb:10) does nothing in production.

findings.claim: The create action never reads params[:alias_level], although the form sends it, so the value is dropped on create.

verifier.reason: In app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:41-52 (patch lines 541-564), `create` sets only `name` and `visible`, while `update` reads `params[:alias_level]` (patch line 580). The client's `asJSON` and `create()` in app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js (patch lines 311-323) send `alias_level` in the POST, so the chosen value is ignored when a group is created. The old `create` also never read `params[:group][:alias_level]`, so the patch carries this gap over rather than introducing it.

findings.claim: add_members does not normalize usernames before lookup, so whitespace or blank entries cause valid users to be skipped.

verifier.reason: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:622-623 splits `usernames` on "," and passes each piece straight to `User.find_by_username`, which only lowercases it (app/models/user.rb:175-177) and never strips whitespace, so a request like "alice, bob" silently skips bob. Blank entries just match nobody and are harmless, and the UI's user-selector joins names with a bare "," (user-selector.js.es6:52), so only hand-written API requests hit this.

findings.claim: The group/members.hbs template contains a stray closing tag with no matching opening tag.

verifier.reason:
app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs:19 has a `` inside the `{{#each}}` loop, after ``, and the template opens no `
` anywhere (lines 1-22). The patch changes only line 6 (`model` to `members`), so this tag was already there.

findings.claim: The SCSS hardcodes the colors #333 and #aaa instead of using SCSS variables.

verifier.reason: The patch adds `.next, .previous { color: #333 !important; &.disabled { color: #aaa !important; } }` at app/assets/stylesheets/common/admin/admin_base.scss:472-475. The same file uses theme variables such as $primary and dark-light-choose in 47 other places, so these two are fixed literal colors that won't follow the theme.

findings.claim: The guard in group/members.hbs checks model, but the loop iterates over members, so the table header can render with no rows.

verifier.reason: After the patch, members.hbs:1 guards on `{{#if model}}`, and the route now sets model to the Group object (group-members.js.es6:363), so the guard is always true. The loop at members.hbs:6 iterates `members`, which `findMembers()` fills asynchronously (group.js:267-271). The 'last seen' header therefore renders with no rows while loading or when the group has no members. Before the patch, model was the members array, so an empty list hid the table.

findings.claim: findMembers builds its URL from the bound, possibly unsaved group name, so after the name is edited, paging/add/remove request /groups/<unsaved-name>/members.json and get a 404.

verifier.reason: Group.findMembers builds its URL as '/groups/' + this.get('name') + '/members.json' (discourse/models/group.js, patch line 261). That `name` is bound to the editable text-field (admin/templates/group.hbs, patch line 153), so next/previous and the reloads after addMembers/removeMember (which post to /admin/groups/<id>) request the unsaved name; one detail is wrong: the server raises InvalidAccess via ensure_can_see!(nil) (groups_controller.rb find_group, lib/guardian/ensure_magic.rb:19), so the request fails with 403, not 404, and if the new name matches another group it lists that group's members.

findings.claim: The commit body is empty, contrary to CONTRIBUTING §5's requirement to describe breaking changes.

verifier.reason: change.patch is a bare diff with no From/Subject/commit header, so the commit message cannot be read from the material here. The claim also misquotes the rule: CONTRIBUTING.md:59-63 asks for a summary line and a detailed description, not specifically a description of breaking changes.

findings.claim: The offset is clamped in the next/previous actions and again in findMembers.

verifier.reason: The offset is clamped twice. The `next` action uses `Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)` (admin-group.js.es6, patch lines 59) and `previous` uses `Math.max(offset - limit, 0)` (patch line 70). `Group.findMembers` then clamps it again with `Math.min(user_count, Math.max(offset, 0))` (discourse/models/group.js, patch line 259).
